subject: Post-call recap — kick off evaluation & schedule demo deep-dive
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Lin <sarah@healthlytics.com>, Luke Chen <luke.chen@healthlytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Apr 2028 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap — kick off evaluation & schedule demo deep-dive

Hi Sarah / Luke —

Really great conversation today — thanks for taking the time. Quick recap from our discovery and proposed next steps so we can lock in an evaluation kickoff and the technical deep-dive: 

Discovery highlights:
- Primary use case: in-app summarization and clinical note generation for provider workflows (ED and ambulatory).
- Key constraints: sub-200ms 95th percentile for short summaries, HIPAA data handling, and on-prem option if we move to production.
- Current stack: Postgres + S3 (de-identified export possible); want minimal data movement during the trial.

Proposed evaluation plan (attached one-pager):
1) 2-week trial with a small prompt pack (15 representative prompts) and 3 success criteria (quality baseline, latency target, integration feasibility).
2) Kickoff session (45m): demo of Redwood runtime, review trial plan, confirm success criteria and data access approach.
3) Tech deep-dive (60m): Ben will walk through integration patterns, KV/prefix caching, and opt-in quantization profiles.

Please review the proposed success criteria below and confirm or edit: 
- Quality: >= 85% pass rate on a small eval prompt set (we'll use your 15 prompts).
- Latency: 95th percentile < 250ms for 512-token requests under a 3 qps profile.
- Integration: Able to complete a sample API call with your de-identified data in 48 hours after kickoff.

Availability — proposed slots (Pacific time):
- Tue Apr 18 — 10:00–10:45 AM PT
- Wed Apr 19 — 2:00–2:45 PM PT
- Thu Apr 20 — 9:00–9:45 AM PT
(If none work, drop a few times that do and we’ll accommodate.)

Attachments: healthlytics-prompt-pack.xlsx (sample prompts), trial-plan-onepager.pdf, healthlytics-data-access-checklist.xlsx
Calendar link to pick a slot: https://cal.redwood.ai/slots/abcd1234

If that looks good, I’ll schedule the kickoff and loop in Ben for the tech deep-dive.

Thanks —
Priyom
Priyom Das | Account Executive 
Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0123

From: Sarah Lin <sarah@healthlytics.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>, Luke Chen <luke.chen@healthlytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Apr 2028 18:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — kick off evaluation & schedule demo deep-dive

Thanks Priyom — appreciate the clear summary. Luke and I reviewed the attachments; the trial approach looks reasonable. A few quick clarifications before we lock time: 

1) Data / Security — for the "sample API call" step, we prefer to start with a de-identified S3 export. Are there any additional vault/KMS steps required on our side?
2) Success criteria — 85% quality pass rate is OK as a starting point. Can you confirm what metric you use for "pass" (ROUGE / human label?) and whether we can review the eval rubric?
3) Attendees — Luke (CTO) will join the kickoff, and we’d like one of your engineers on the tech deep-dive (Ben?).

For times, the 2:00–2:45 PM Wed Apr 19 PT slot works best for both of us. If Ben can make that, we’re happy to lock it.

Thanks —
Sarah
Sarah Lin | Head of Product
HealthLytics
sarah@healthlytics.com

Thanks — I can join Wed Apr 19 at 2:00 PM PT. I’ll take the lead on the tech deep-dive and cover the following: 
- Integration patterns (server-to-server API examples, streaming vs blocking)
- Caching + KV usage to meet latency SLOs
- Suggested model variants and quantization profiles for the trial (I recommend trying an INT8-quantized gpt-style variant and one float16 baseline)

Sarah — on the data access question: the de-identified S3 export is ideal. If you prefer no data movement, we can run a short on-prem exercise during the trial but that does add ~1 week to setup. I’ll review the data-access checklist and follow up directly on any required IAM/KMS steps.
